clue.text: Evil women apprehended without notice initially

indicators.note: without tells us to take a letter away from the word for apprehended

parts.note: nicked is British slang for arrested

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word notice

explanation.surface: A wicked gang of women is arrested in a sudden raid with no warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehended' is British slang 'nicked'; 'without' and 'initially' drop the opening letter of notice from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are plain adjectives for morally bad or sinful behaviour.

clue.text: Advantage of trendy husband coated in something magical

indicators.note: coated in means those letters are wrapped inside the magic item

parts.note: a wand is the magician's tool
hip means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A fashionable man gains an edge by being covered in magic.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold the upper hand is to have control, an advantage over others.

clue.text: Draw near to support rally

parts.note: to come is to draw near, approach
to back is to support

explanation.surface: Supporters approach to give backing at a political rally.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally in sport is a recovery from a losing position, a revival.

clue.text: Number entering illegal gang have tattoos to start with

indicators.note: to start with tells us to take the opening letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: Those joining a criminal gang must first get tattoos.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal number, one more than seven.

clue.text: Practice suffering at work

parts.note: a trial is an ordeal, a period of suffering
a machine that is running is at work, operating

explanation.surface: Someone's daily practice is a misery endured in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or test run before the real thing is a form of practice.

clue.text: Artist to outline daily grind

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
to trace is to draw an outline

explanation.surface: A painter sketches the routine of everyday work.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitive struggle of working life is the routine people call the daily slog.

clue.text: A lean colt bolting suddenly

indicators.note: a bolting horse runs off wildly, so the letters scatter

explanation.surface: A thin young horse suddenly breaks away and runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done all in one go is abrupt and happens without warning.

clue.text: Vehicle coming up to get queen's jockeys?

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen, plus 's

explanation.surface: A royal coach draws up for the queen's riders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns CAR into RAC. The question mark admits that the racers are jockeys only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Jockeys are people who race horses, so the term fits loosely, as the question mark concedes.

clue.text: Rovers curse about keeping ball on side initially

indicators.note: keeping means the curse holds the ball inside it
about means the word for curse is turned round

parts.note: damn is a curse
O is shaped like a ball

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of side

explanation.surface: A football team called Rovers swears about keeping possession on their side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns DAMN into NMAD, which 'keeping' wraps round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderers with no fixed home are people who roam.

clue.text: Mother and child preparing fruit

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A mother and her child prepare some fruit together.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small dark purple plum.

clue.text: Newcomer timing mare running without tail

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move into a new order
without tail means the last letter of mare is dropped

explanation.surface: A new arrival at the stables is clocking a horse as it gallops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without tail' cuts mare to MAR; 'running' then rearranges TIMING plus MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has recently settled in a new country is a newcomer there.

clue.text: Look about to get posh male doctor

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
C stands for circa, Latin for about
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech

explanation.surface: Someone is told to search for a well-to-do gentleman physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in doctor who covers for an absent colleague is a familiar British term for a temporary practitioner.

clue.text: Sailor in belted dress

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the word for belted

parts.note: belted means struck hard, hit
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor wears a dress gathered at the waist with a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is the distinctive garment of a monk or nun, so a form of dress.

clue.text: Exhausted and tense, rest head uneasily

indicators.note: uneasily hints at restless movement, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone worn out and on edge lays their head down but cannot settle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneasily' rearranges T together with REST HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Shattered is everyday British slang for utterly tired out.

clue.text: Study revolutionary change in part of service

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the word for study is read backwards

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a turn is a change of direction or state

explanation.surface: A political student plots radical change.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturn is one of the divisions of the night office of matins in church worship.

clue.text: Unobserved nun woken roughly around start of benediction

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the other piece
roughly suggests a rough, disordered rearrangement of the letters
start of takes the first letter of benediction

explanation.surface: A nun is shaken awake just as the blessing begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges NUN WOKEN, and 'around' puts that round B.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without anyone knowing is unseen, unknown to others.

clue.text: Heroines oddly missing for long periods

indicators.note: oddly missing means the letters in odd positions are lost, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Female heroes, strangely, have been absent from the story for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeons are immensely long stretches of time, spelt here the American way.

clue.text: Runner runs mile with one shoe, half having been lost in fight

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: half having been lost means only the first half of shoe remains

explanation.surface: An athlete runs a mile in one shoe after losing the other in a scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief minor clash between small groups is a skirmish.

clue.text: Lie given in order to entice

indicators.note: in order suggests the letters must be put into a proper new arrangement

explanation.surface: A falsehood is told in order to lure someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone by flattery or deception is to lure them in.

clue.text: Help out in a punt

parts.note: a punt is British slang for a bet or gamble

explanation.surface: Someone gives a hand with a boat on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a flat river boat; here it means a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist, usually in wrongdoing, so to help out.

clue.text: Bit of tainted foreign dough causes upset

indicators.note: bit of picks just the first letter of tainted

parts.note: dough is slang for money; the rouble is Russian currency

explanation.surface: A tainted bit of imported bread dough makes someone ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to disturb or worry them.

clue.text: Holiday on popular train

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A holiday trip taken on a well-loved railway service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway noun but is the verb used of horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To break in a horse is to train it to accept a rider.

clue.text: Urban kerb-crawler accommodates one working in city

indicators.note: accommodates means the clue words house the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A town kerb-crawler gives someone a lift to their job in the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'city' is the City of London, the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier is typical of those employed in the City of London, the financial district.

clue.text: Comic sketches featuring king in women's clothing

indicators.note: featuring means the sketches include the king inside them

parts.note: skits are short comic sketches
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A comedy routine shows a king dressed in women's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirts are garments hanging from the waist, worn chiefly by women.

clue.text: Head of farm gets more unusual feed

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of farm

parts.note: odder means stranger, more unusual

explanation.surface: The farm manager buys a stranger kind of animal feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder is food such as hay given to livestock.

clue.text: Rubbish feathers on sale

parts.note: to rubbish something is to criticise it, to knock it
down is the soft fine plumage of birds

explanation.surface: Worthless feathers are being sold off cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockdown prices are greatly reduced ones, as for goods offered in a sale.

clue.text: Steel plane returns with king on board

indicators.note: on board means the king is carried inside the other piece
returns means the word for plane is read backwards

parts.note: plane as an adjective means flat or level, even
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A steel aircraft comes back carrying a monarch as passenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' makes NEVE from EVEN; 'on board' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To steel yourself is to summon courage, to brace your resolve.

clue.text: Mad teachers get extremely testy

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme, outer letters of testy

explanation.surface: Angry teachers become very irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy or eccentric behaviour is described as nuts.

clue.text: Jumper goes over edges of dyke in cowboy show

indicators.note: goes over means the jumper covers or surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: edges of picks the first and last letters of dyke

explanation.surface: A kangaroo leaps a ditch during a Wild West exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a sweater; it is the kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public exhibition of riding and roping skills by cowboys.

clue.text: Swimming across creek regularly is inspiring

indicators.note: across means the swimming word stretches over the other letters

parts.note: bathing is swimming in open water

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of creek

explanation.surface: A swim over a small stream is an uplifting experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' looks like 'uplifting' but means drawing breath in; 'across' and 'regularly' are the containment and alternate-letter signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiring literally means drawing air into the lungs, so taking a breath.

clue.text: Way Mountie gets man from elsewhere

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
a Canadian Mountie is a mounted police officer, akin to a ranger

explanation.surface: A Canadian mounted policeman comes across a man from out of town on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider who comes from another place is unknown to the locals.

clue.text: Fruit with really cheesy covering

indicators.note: covering means the two words cover, and so conceal, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit coated in something very cheesy.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sweet Chinese fruit with white flesh inside a rough red skin.
